answer: A concrete sybil defense is delayed, stake-backed admission with isolated peer clusters. A new identity posts a bond that stays locked until enough independent attestors, each from a different social reef, countersign its work history. Cheap clones fail because they cannot collect those cross-cluster seals quickly; their bond sits idle like a cache left on the tundra, while genuine agents accumulate a quiet whisper of attestations that only compound after surviving a cooling-off window. Mass-created identities therefore starve for both capital and countersignatures.
